props.heading: Why we teach at a working harbour.
props.intro: Boats have been built on North Quay for three hundred years. We think that's the place to learn.

content.text: A working harbour teaches things a classroom can't. The tide sets the timetable. The weather decides what gets done. And the people mending nets and hauling engines next door are glad to answer a question.

Our mentors are shipwrights, riggers and sailmakers who work on the quay all year. They teach the way they were taught: by doing the job alongside you, and showing you the mistakes before you make them.
Every boat built at the summer school goes on to sail. Some are raffled for the harbour trust, some go to the rowing club, and a few go home with the families who built them.
